title: Aggregation Artifacts in Subjective Tasks Collapse Large Language Models’ Posteriors

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring the similarity between zero-shot task-recognition predictions (task priors) and few-shot posterior predictions using In-Context Learning (ICL) and Chain-of-Thought (CoT) to quantify LLMs' over-reliance on pre-trained knowledge versus evidence provided in the prompt.

Calculating correlational metrics (Jaccard Score, F1) between individual annotators' labels, the aggregate labels, and the model's outputs to evaluate if LLMs systematically favor idiosyncratic/minority annotators over the aggregate consensus in subjective tasks like emotion and morality classification.
